## Design roles

Each part does a job for the person. These are the jobs, as questions the part answers.

<div class="odv-am-rolelist"><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Containment</b> What holds this?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Layering</b> What sits on top?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Hierarchy</b> What do you read first?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Readability</b> Can you read it?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Emphasis</b> Where does the eye go?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Meaning</b> What state is it in?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Affordance</b> Can you act on it?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Feedback</b> Did it respond?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Focus</b> Where is the keyboard?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Grouping</b> What belongs together?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Reach</b> Can you hit it?</span></div>

## How the decisions reach each part

Each part follows a chain: an answer about the product, the rule it set, the token that carries it, and the value you see. The numbers match the drawing.

<section class="odv-am-card" id="part-1-2"><div class="odv-am-img wide"><span class="odv-am-assetbox"><img class="odv-am-asset" src="/anatomy/dense-data/scroll-area/card-1.png" alt="Scrollbar: 1, 2" loading="lazy"/></span></div><div class="odv-am-body"><header><i class="odv-am-n">1</i><i class="odv-am-n">2</i><b>Scrollbar</b><span class="odv-am-role" title="Can you hit it?">Reach</span><span class="odv-am-role" title="Did it respond?">Feedback</span><span class="odv-am-role" title="Can you act on it?">Affordance</span></header><ul class="odv-am-tree"><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Shape · Which shape roles does it need? → Controls, badges and containers</div><div class="odv-am-why">Badges sit in columns and need their own corner.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>border-width.default</code><span>→</span><code>scrollbar.border-width</code><span class="odv-am-val">1px</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. The part is the same in every scheme."><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="11" height="11" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m11 10 3 3"/><path d="M6.5 21A3.5 3.5 0 1 0 3 17.5a2.62 2.62 0 0 1-.708 1.792A1 1 0 0 0 3 21z"/><path d="M9.969 17.031 21.378 5.624a1 1 0 0 0-3.002-3.002L6.967 14.031"/></svg>By scheme</span></div><div class="odv-am-lines"><div><b>Pick</b> border-width.1</div></div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>radius.round</code><span>→</span><code>thumb.radius</code><span class="odv-am-val">9999px</span></div><div class="odv-am-lines"><div><b>Pick</b> radius.full</div></div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>color.border.default</code><span>→</span><code>thumb.background</code><span class="odv-am-val">#DDE2EA · dark #3D4655</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. The part is the same in every scheme."><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="11" height="11" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m11 10 3 3"/><path d="M6.5 21A3.5 3.5 0 1 0 3 17.5a2.62 2.62 0 0 1-.708 1.792A1 1 0 0 0 3 21z"/><path d="M9.969 17.031 21.378 5.624a1 1 0 0 0-3.002-3.002L6.967 14.031"/></svg>By scheme</span></div><div class="odv-am-why">Quiet edges and dividers. Decorative, so it has no contrast minimum.</div><div class="odv-am-lines"><div><b>Pick</b> neutral.200: a quiet line that stays visible on every surface it meets (lowest 1.22:1, on surface.canvas). It decorates, so it holds no contrast minimum.</div><div><b>Dark</b> neutral.200: a quiet line that stays visible on every surface it meets (lowest 1.82:1, on surface.default). It decorates, so it holds no contrast minimum.</div><div><b>Shares the step with</b> disabled.border. Changing this pick moves only what reads color.border.default.</div></div></li></ul></div></section>

## For agents

Agents get this same anatomy: every part, its roles, whether it is required, the tokens it reads and the decisions behind them.

- **From an AI agent:** call the `get_anatomy` tool on the Open DS MCP server, with this scheme and `scroll-area`.
- **From a terminal:** `npx open-ds anatomy dense-data scroll-area`
